• Socialistic Principles
• Gandhian Principles
• Liberal-Intellectual Principles
These principles aim to promote social and economic justice.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Directive Principles are broadly categorized into Socialistic, Gandhian, and Liberal-Intellectual principles.
Socialistic Principles primarily aim to establish social and economic justice in society.
Article 38 and Article 39 lay the foundation for people's welfare, equal justice, and adequate livelihood.
Article 39A provides free legal aid, while Article 43A mandates worker participation in industrial management.
Articles 41, 42, 43, and 47 deal with workers' rights, humane working conditions, living wages, and improving public health.
Article 39A (Free legal aid) and Article 43A (Workers' participation in management) are frequently asked in Indian competitive exams.
Article 38 is specifically tested regarding the State's duty to promote the welfare of the people.
Article 47 is often cited in questions related to public health, nutrition standards, and living standards.

blocks.content:
These principles aim to promote social and economic justice.
Important Articles:
• Article 38 – Promote welfare of the people.
• Article 39 – Equal justice and adequate means of livelihood.
• Article 39A – Free legal aid.
• Article 41 – Right to work, education, and public assistance.
• Article 42 – Just and humane conditions of work.
• Article 43 – Living wage for workers.
• Article 43A – Participation of workers in management.
• Article 47 – Improve nutrition, standard of living, and public health.
